Does Mathlib have any formalization of strongly continuous one-parameter semigroups on Banach spaces? Following Engel-Nagel, One-Parameter Semigroups for Linear Evolution Equations (GTM 194, Springer 2000), Ch. II, I'm looking for:

  • The definition: a family S(t) of bounded linear operators with S(0) = 1, S(s+t) = S(s) ∘ S(t), and t ↦ S(t)x continuous
  • The infinitesimal generator Ax = lim_{t→0⁺} (S(t)x - x)/t
  • The growth bound ‖S(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt}
  • The resolvent R(λ) = ∫₀^∞ e^{-λt} S(t) dt

I have a formalization of these with the forward direction of Hille-Yosida (resolvent bound) and would be interested in contributing if this isn't already covered.

The Hille-Yosida theorem would be a nice addition to mathlib! In principle, contributions are very welcome.
To avoid surprises later: are you aware of mathlib's AI policy? At the moment, opening a PR with AI-generated code is a net negative (for the reasons explained there). Hand-written PRs, with the desire to learn, are welcome.

The code will be almost all generated by AI, yes, and vetted by me. I will make efforts to conform to mathlib standards including multiple revisions but these will be aided by AI. If that is not welcome then I will send it elsewhere.

How about this: I extract out the definitions from my formalization, go over them by hand, and submit those. Then we review and reach agreement on that. This way we will standardize the definitions, I can use my AI proofs, and others can come along and write handcrafted proofs if they like. Sound good?

I personally think that this sounds like a good idea for now, but I don't speak for the maintainers. In fact I think this would be an interesting experiment.

Note that if you do PR definitions and then in review it's suggested that the definitions be substantially changed then this might break your proofs. You can have one of several reactions here; the most naive, in some sense, is "that's fine, I change the definitions for mathlib and then get AI to fix up my proofs" but it's been pointed out that it's easier to make a mess than to tidy up a mess, and this could be a failure point for AI (at least today; perhaps things depend a lot on exactly how much the definitions get changed). If mathlib then ends up with different definitions to the ones you're using then this represents a possibly dangerous divergence.

If your definitions go through unscathed then your observation that you can use your AI proofs and more fool mathlib for not accepting them will be an interesting test too -- mathlib's reluctance is in part, I believe, due to the fact that the maintainers are concerned about the maintenance burden of AI-generated proofs. Do you intend to keep your AI work up to date with mathlib? The test then is to see if you can do this and to see how much keeping up costs you, and how easy it is, with perhaps suboptimal proofs. And if you decide not to keep up then again this represents a divergence, the consequences of which are yet to be understood.

Yes, the idea is to accept and work with the definitions as they evolve in mathlib, and use the AIs to keep my own work up to date. BTW I'm not proposing this primarily to get it in mathlib, I'm doing it because I want to use these results in my ongoing work and I will be happy to hand off some of the maintenance to mathlib! If proofs magically appear there then I will switch over to them.
I would be interested to get C0C_0C0​-semigroups in mathlib. From what I know of the theory it seems very suitable for formalization.
Hi ! , i haven't found von neuman algebras libs or Fourier analysis (or related ones), it would be nice to have any, specially for the hydrodynamics, Sobolev spaces ?, any help is appreciated !
